newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities ended higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities ended higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended higher across the board in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Friday.

"Treasury bill yields ended slightly lower today but bond prices ended higher across the board. These higher rates did not have an impact on the market. The interbank rate eased slightly. Volume was only moderate still due to the New Year holidays," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.23/1.18 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 1.40/1.35 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.73/1.68 percent against 2.10/2.05 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.75/98.80 from Tuesday's close of S$98.45/98.50, September 2001 at S$97.58/97.63 versus S$97.40/97.45 and June 2003 at S$95.58/95.63 against S$95.40/95.45.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 2-1/2 2-3/8 percent from Tuesday's 2-3/4 2-1/2 percent.
